# When --opt maps=true, Go-emitting platforms inject //line directives
# before each statement so the Go compiler attributes errors and stack
# traces back to the original SNGL source.
#
# gc resolves a relative //line path against the directory of the file
# carrying it, so the path is written relative to the output. Built from a
# subdirectory, so "../src/app.sngl" is distinguishable from both the
# invocation path and a bare basename.

mkdir src
cp app.sngl src/app.sngl
rm app.sngl

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt=main=true --opt=maps=true --out=out src/app.sngl
exists out/model.go

# Named as reached from out/, where model.go lives.
grep '//line \.\./src/app\.sngl:' out/model.go

# And it resolves to the real file.
exists out/../src/app.sngl

# An absolute path would resolve, but only on the machine that built it.
! grep '//line /' out/model.go

# Sanity: without maps the directive is absent.
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt=main=true --out=out2 src/app.sngl
exists out2/model.go
! grep '//line ' out2/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component main node {
    var count = 0
    text(value=string(count))
    button(text="+", @click { count += 1 })
}

app.window {
    main
}
